title: Field Evaluation Fast-Path and Rollback Playbook
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview
========
This playbook defines a minimal-latency, low-friction 'fast path' for promoting model candidates to limited field traffic and the precise automated and manual rollback procedures that must be applied when regressions or infrastructure anomalies are detected. It combines evaluation harness checks, prompt-set sampling, quality guardrails, and quantization verification into a single operational flow so teams can ship changes quickly while bounding user impact.

Scope and applicability
----------------------
- Applies to: model promotions for Redwood Hosted and Dedicated flows where a model variant is introduced as a canary (traffic <= 5%).
- Not covered: full-scale (>=50%) rollouts, private air-gapped on-prem packages (see onprem-packaging docs).
- Intended audience: Applied ML engineers, runtime owners, SRE oncall.

Definitions
-----------
- Fast-path: a shortened promotion pipeline intended for low-risk model updates (bug fixes, quant tweaks, minor prompt-template changes).
- Canary cohort: a small, deterministic subset (~1–5%) of live traffic selected by routing policy (user sampling or route-based split).
- Regression: any measured drop below defined quality guardrail thresholds or breach of latency/cost SLOs for the canary cohort.

Prerequisites and gating checks
-------------------------------
Before triggering fast-path promotion, the candidate must have passed all items below:
1) Offline eval harness smoke: unit tests, 3 synthetic slices, and at least one few-shot stress benchmark (see eval-harness checklist).
2) Quantization sanity (if applicable): per-workload quant profile applied and run for 2k in-distribution samples with top-k accuracy delta <= configured budget (default 0.6%).
3) Prompt-set sanity: prioritized prompt subset (N=500) passes coverage/edge checks including tokenization stability and injection-resilience.
4) Telemetry hooks: trace IDs, request provenance, and per-request scoring metadata must be emitted by runtime (see runbook snippet below).
5) Canary config declared in deployment manifest and approved by owning team.

Ownership matrix
----------------
- Model Owner: prepares candidate artifacts, offline eval results, quant profile.
- Runtime Owner: validates tracer and metrics integration; creates canary routing.
- SRE Oncall: watches health dashboards during rollout window; empowered to trigger automated rollback.
- Applied ML (on-call): performs prompt-level triage and quality assessment.

Fast-path rollout procedure (step-by-step)
-----------------------------------------
1) Pre-flight (T-30m):
   - Verify rollout window on calendar and oncall availability.
   - Confirm alerting receiver list and escalation policy.
   - Attach the candidate release notes and quick-check results to the rollout ticket.
2) Canary enable (T0):
   - Update routing policy: add candidate variant with weight 1% (or route by hash to specific user cohort).
   - Start a 15-minute passive monitoring phase before enabling synthetic probing.
3) Probe + score (T+15m):
   - Launch synthetic probe job that replays 1k high-priority prompts sampled from the prioritized prompt-set.
   - Supply probes with annotated golden outputs where available and compute the following metrics: Quality Score (Q), Response Stability Index (RSI), and Safety Flag rate (S).
4) Evaluation windows (T+15m..T+60m):
   - 15 minute early window: if any metric breaches critical thresholds (see thresholds table) trigger immediate rollback.
   - 60 minute extended window: require metrics to remain within warning thresholds for automated promotion to 5% or handoff for broader rollout.
5) Promotion or rollback:
   - If all checks pass for 60 minutes, optionally promote to 5% and repeat observation. If checks fail, execute rollback (automated path preferred).

Automated rollback triggers and thresholds
-----------------------------------------
- These thresholds are minimums; product or compliance teams may impose tighter limits.

| Class | Metric | Immediate rollback threshold | Warning threshold | Notes |
|-------|--------|-----------------------------:|------------------:|-------|
| Quality | Quality Score (Q) delta vs baseline | >= 2.0% absolute drop | 0.8% drop | Q is a weighted F1/semantic-similarity composite for the prompt-set. |
| Safety | Safety Flag rate | > 0.2% absolute increase | > 0.05% increase | Includes toxic/PII/excess-leak flags from guardrail classifiers. |
| Latency | P95 request latency | > 250 ms increase | > 100 ms increase | Measured server-side, region-specific. |
| Error | 5xx rate | > 0.1% absolute | > 0.02% | Includes malformed responses and rejection-rate increases. |
| Cost | Per-token cost | > 20% increase | > 8% | For quantized vs baseline comparison. |

Alerting and observability configuration (examples)
--------------------------------------------------
- Dashboards: canary model panel, per-prompt drift stream, error-by-slice heatmap, latency heatmap by region.
- Prometheus alert examples (PromQL):
  - Quality drop (pseudo):
    sum(rate(quality_failures_total{model="candidate",cohort="canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(request_total{model="candidate",cohort="canary"}[5m])) > 0.02
  - Latency spike (P95):
    histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{model="candidate"}[5m])) by (le)) - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{model="baseline"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.25

Rollback procedures
-------------------
Automated rollback (preferred):
1) Alert triggers automated rollback lambda which immediately flips routing weight of candidate to 0 and routes traffic back to baseline variant.
2) System creates a rollback incident ticket with prefilled diagnostic context (metrics snapshots, top failing prompts, recent traces).
3) Notification posted to #oncall-alerts and relevant team Slack channels.

Manual rollback (if automation unavailable):
1) Runtime owner runs: 
   rwdctl rollout set-weight --model candidate --variant v42 --weight 0 --reason "fast-path rollback"
2) Confirm traffic normalized and watch for rate/latency stabilization for 10 minutes.
3) SRE records incident and attaches diagnostic artifacts.

Triage checklist after rollback
------------------------------
- Capture the top 200 canary requests (persist to secure bucket) and run them through: baseline, candidate, and offline eval harness.
- Produce a prompt-failure inventory that categorizes failures into: Safety, Coherence, Hallucination, Latency/Timeout, Infrastructure error.
- Run automated blame-assistant bisect if regression appears after a baseline-within-memory window change (see automated-regression-bisect doc).
- If quantization implicated, revert to float variant and re-run the quant sanity job.

Prompt-set and evaluation artifacts to attach to the rollback ticket
------------------------------------------------------------------
- Prioritized prompt set subset (500 samples) used for probes.
- Top 200 live canary requests (scrubbed for PII) and the annotated human labels if available.
- Offline eval harness logs and per-slice metrics.
- Quant profile metadata and tensor-level warnings (if used).

Quantization-specific guardrails
-------------------------------
- If candidate uses an updated quant profile: require a targeted micro-benchmark: 5k tokens replay with token-level divergence tracking, and a top-k token stability metric.
- Rollback if token-stability > 1.0% or hallucination proxies spike.

Runbook snippets and tooling
---------------------------
- Example canary YAML (deployment manifest):
  ---
  canary:
    variant: v42
    weight: 0.01
    sampling: user_hash_mod_100 < 1
    probe_job: probe-scheduler/field-probe-v42
    observability_tags:
      cohort: canary
      owner: sofia-patel

- CLI quick commands:
  - Promote to 1%: rwdctl deploy promote --model my-model --variant v42 --weight 0.01
  - Force rollback: rwdctl deploy promote --model my-model --variant baseline --weight 1.0 --reason "rollback"

Post-incident learnings and permanent actions
---------------------------------------------
1) If rollback was due to model quality: create a remediation PR in the model-onboarding tracker with items: prompt-set gaps, new unit tests, and expanded synthetic probes.
2) If rollback was due to infra: raise an SRE hotfix ticket for runtime or kernel-level failure and schedule a game-day if recurrence >2x/month.
3) If quantization is repeatedly implicated: add the workload to the per-workload quant tuner queue and require a shadow rollout before field fast-path.

Safety and compliance notes
--------------------------
- All captured canary requests used for triage must be scrubbed by the automated PII scrubber before attaching to tickets.
- If customer-sensitive content is present, route materials to the security-and-compliance team and mark the incident as restricted.

Appendix: quick play summary (cheat-sheet)
-----------------------------------------
1) Preconditions: offline smoke ✅, quant sanity ✅, tracer hooks ✅.
2) Start canary: 1% weight, passive monitor 15m.
3) Run probes: 1k prioritized prompts, compute Q/RSI/S.
4) If any critical thresholds breached -> auto rollback.
5) If stable 60m -> promote to 5% and repeat.
